Analysis: Hypothesis 1 presents a novel diagnostic strategy by integrating exosomal miRNAs and ctDNA methylation biomarkers, employing advanced detection methods and machine learning to achieve early HCC detection, including in AFP-negative cases. It is grounded in existing methodologies that are relatively well established, making it more plausible and straightforward to test. The technical challenges and specificity issues highlighted can be addressed with careful study design and standardization, while its diagnostic nature involves minimal safety concerns. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 involves a more complex mechanistic pathway linking cytokine-induced glycosyltransferase activity to AFP glycosylation and oncogenic signaling. Though innovative, it lacks robust preliminary evidence, has more intricate experimental challenges, and incorporates safety concerns related to CRISPR gene editing. Overall, Hypothesis 1 is superior in terms of novelty, plausibility, testability, and safety.
